title: Trump BLS commissioner posts bigoted content under pseudonyms
description_short: Trump BLS commissioner posts bigoted content under pseudonyms
description_medium: CNN reported that E.J. Antoni, Trump’s nominee to lead the Bureau of Labor Statistics, had posted bigoted and sexually degrading material on since-deleted Twitter accounts. The posts, made under several aliases between roughly 2017 and 2020, included attacks on Kamala Harris, homophobic remarks, conspiracy theories, and insults aimed at Trump’s critics. Antoni did not publicly acknowledge the accounts in the report.
description_long: The reporting concerned online posts attributed to E.J. Antoni before Trump nominated him to lead the Bureau of Labor Statistics. CNN said it matched several since-deleted Twitter aliases to the same account using biographical details and reviewed posts from approximately 2017 through 2020. The material included sexually degrading comments about Kamala Harris, derogatory remarks about gay people, conspiracy theories, and crude attacks on critics of Donald Trump. The posts surfaced as Antoni, then an economist at the Heritage Foundation, was being considered for a role overseeing federal labor statistics. That timing brought scrutiny to the administration’s choice and to how the nominee’s public record fit the responsibilities of a statistical agency. The article reports the content and CNN’s attribution process; it does not establish that Antoni authored every post through an independent court finding. Because the input title calls him a commissioner while the source described him as Trump’s pick or nominee, this account identifies his status at the time of the reporting rather than implying Senate confirmation.

preserved_fields.title: Trump BLS commissioner posts bigoted content under pseudonyms
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump BLS commissioner posts bigoted content under pseudonyms

notes: CNN reports that it linked the pseudonymous accounts to Antoni and describes the posts; its article identifies him as Trump’s nominee, not a confirmed commissioner.

title: Trump: The turbulent 15 months of Trump’s unlikely US intelligence director
description_short: Trump: The turbulent 15 months of Trump’s unlikely US intelligence director
description_medium: The turbulent 15 months of Trump’s unlikely US intelligence director. The ex-Democrat without an intelligence background took many actions seemingly meant to flatter Trump This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, legal development, documented relationship, or policy consequence linked directly or indirectly to Trump. The downstream effects include institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: Tulsi Gabbard’s tenure as director of national intelligence lasted about fifteen months and drew scrutiny over her conduct and the handling of intelligence. The Guardian described her as an unconventional choice for the job and reported that she was largely sidelined while Trump launched attacks on Venezuela and Iran. Gabbard announced in May 2026 that she would leave the post on June 30, saying she wanted to support her husband during treatment for a rare cancer. PBS NewsHour published the resignation letter and noted the scrutiny surrounding her time leading the intelligence community. These reports establish the appointment’s unusual character, the limited role attributed to her during major military decisions, and the timing and stated reason for her departure. They do not by themselves substantiate every interpretation that a particular decision was intended to flatter Trump. The long account therefore records the documented tenure and controversy while leaving motive claims attributed to the reporting and open to further evidence.

title: Trump Calls Republican Senator Murkowski a "Traitor" for AG Vote
description_short: Trump Calls Republican Senator Murkowski a "Traitor" for AG Vote
description_medium: Hours after Todd Blanche's confirmation, Trump attacked Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski on Truth Social, calling her a "traitor" and "owned" for voting against his AG pick. He posted a video juxtaposing Murkowski with Merrick Garland authorizing the Mar-a-Lago search warrant. Murkowski had cited concerns about Blanche's handling of the Epstein files, the sweeping Trump family immunity protections, and "repeated targeting of individuals ranging from former administration staff to sitting U.S. Senators."
description_long: After the Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as attorney general in a 50–49 overnight vote, Trump attacked Senator Lisa Murkowski on Truth Social for voting against him. The Independent reported that Trump called the Alaska Republican a “traitor” and criticized her for having supported Merrick Garland’s confirmation. Murkowski and Senator Susan Collins were the two Republicans who opposed Blanche. Murkowski had raised concerns about the Justice Department’s handling of the Epstein files, protections for Trump and his family, and what she described as targeting of political opponents. The dispute followed confirmation of a former Trump personal lawyer to lead the department and showed how a vote against the president’s nominee became a public loyalty test. The article records Trump’s accusation and Murkowski’s stated concerns; it does not establish that her vote was improper or that the department acted unlawfully. This account keeps the criticism attributed to each participant and distinguishes a political attack from evidence about the department’s future conduct.

title: IRS Workers Union Sues to Block Trump Family Tax Audit Immunity Order
description_short: IRS Workers Union Sues to Block Trump Family Tax Audit Immunity Order
description_medium: The National Treasury Employees Union sued to challenge the retroactive immunity deal shielding Trump, his sons, and the Trump Organization from tax audits for all conduct before May 2026. The lawsuit argues the arrangement violates the Internal Revenue Code prohibition on presidential interference with tax audits and constitutes an unconstitutional emolument.
description_long: The National Treasury Employees Union asked a federal court to block an agreement shielding Donald Trump, his sons, and the Trump Organization from certain tax audits. Associated Press reporting said the union argued that the arrangement would force IRS employees to choose between complying with a political directive and following tax law. The amended lawsuit challenged the retroactive scope of the deal and raised statutory and constitutional objections. It followed a settlement granting immunity for audits of conduct before May 2026, according to the supplied account. The dispute was not resolved when the suit was filed: the union was asking a judge to intervene, and the audit protections remained in place at that point. The case raised a conflict-of-interest concern because the agreement affected the president’s own tax exposure and his family’s business, while the employees responsible for administering audits were represented by the plaintiff union. The allegations in the complaint are claims for the court to assess, not a ruling that the arrangement was unlawful.

preserved_fields.description_short: IRS Workers Union Sues to Block Trump Family Tax Audit Immunity Order

title: confirms that he and Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro spoke via telephone earlier
description_short: President Trump confirms that he and Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro spoke via telephone earlier in the month
description_medium: Donald Trump confirmed on November 30, 2025, that he had spoken by phone with Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, but declined to describe the discussion. Reuters reported that The New York Times had first reported the call and a possible meeting. Trump said he would not characterize the conversation as good or bad.
description_long: Trump acknowledged the phone conversation with Maduro while tensions between Washington and Caracas were rising. Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One on November 30, he answered yes when asked whether he had spoken with the Venezuelan president, then declined to provide details or characterize the call as successful or unsuccessful. Reuters reported that The New York Times had first disclosed the conversation and said the leaders had discussed a possible meeting in the United States. The confirmation came amid Trump’s public pressure on Venezuela and administration statements about military operations in the region, so it showed diplomacy and confrontation occurring at the same time. The source does not establish what was agreed, whether a meeting was scheduled, or whether the call changed U.S. policy. The event is a confirmed communication between the two presidents, while the substance and consequences remain undisclosed. Keeping those limits clear avoids turning an acknowledged call into claims about a deal or a shift in relations.

preserved_fields.title: confirms that he and Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro spoke via telephone earlier
preserved_fields.description_short: President Trump confirms that he and Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro spoke via telephone earlier in the month

notes: Reuters reports Trump’s confirmation, his refusal to disclose the call’s substance, and the earlier report that a possible meeting was discussed; no agreement was confirmed.

title: The US Coast Guard seized a sixth sanctioned oil tanker in the
description_short: The US Coast Guard seized a sixth sanctioned oil tanker in the Caribbean Sea, the tanker reportedly had ties to Venezuela
description_medium: The Coast Guard seized the tanker Veronica in the Caribbean in an operation U.S. officials described as enforcing sanctions on vessels linked to Venezuelan oil. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said the ship had passed through Venezuelan waters and was operating against the administration’s quarantine. Officials said the boarding occurred without incident.
description_long: The Associated Press reported that U.S. forces boarded and seized the tanker Veronica in the Caribbean, describing it as the sixth sanctioned oil tanker taken during the campaign against vessels tied to Venezuela. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said the ship had previously traveled through Venezuelan waters and was operating in defiance of the administration’s quarantine of sanctioned vessels. U.S. Southern Command said Marines and sailors launched from the aircraft carrier USS Gerald R. Ford to support a Coast Guard tactical team; officials said the seizure was completed without incident. The account shows the use of maritime enforcement and military support in the administration’s pressure campaign over Venezuelan oil. It does not independently establish the ship’s cargo ownership or a court finding about sanctions violations. The seizure’s place in a wider series gives the event context, but the government’s characterization of the vessel and the legality of the broader operation should remain attributed to officials unless separately adjudicated.

preserved_fields.description_short: The US Coast Guard seized a sixth sanctioned oil tanker in the Caribbean Sea, the tanker reportedly had ties to Venezuela

title: Trump Claims Wind Turbine Noise Causes Cancer
description_short: Trump Claims Wind Turbine Noise Causes Cancer
description_medium: At a Republican fundraising dinner on April 2, 2019, Trump said wind-turbine noise causes cancer and claimed nearby wind farms could cut home values by 75 percent. The Washington Post reported the remarks as part of a speech criticizing Hillary Clinton’s support for wind power. The cancer claim was unsupported; the story did not document a medical finding backing it.
description_long: Trump made the remarks during the National Republican Congressional Committee’s spring dinner, while criticizing Hillary Clinton’s support for wind energy. The Washington Post reported that he claimed homes near windmills lost 75 percent of their value and repeated the assertion that turbine noise causes cancer. The speech turned a policy argument about renewable power into a broader attack on wind energy. The article treated the cancer statement as unsupported and situated it among Trump’s repeated claims about climate and renewable energy. That distinction is important: the record documents what the president said, not a medical effect established by evidence. The property-value figure was also presented as Trump’s claim rather than as a measured outcome in the story. Wind turbines can raise separate local concerns about siting, noise, and property impacts, but those do not validate a cancer claim. The event illustrates how false or unsubstantiated health assertions can enter political debate about energy policy and influence public discussion of climate measures.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Claims Wind Turbine Noise Causes Cancer
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Claims Wind Turbine Noise Causes Cancer

notes: The Washington Post reports Trump’s April 2, 2019 dinner remarks about cancer and home values; it presents these as his claims, not established medical or property findings.
